title: Circuit gate-processing loop
statement: Let $C$ be a family of directed acyclic circuits, and let $n,i,B$ be natural numbers and $[?]$ be a Boolean parameter $	ext{lm}$. Assume the circuit $C_n$ has its gate argument lists sorted in strictly increasing order and satisfies $	ext{output}(C_n)+1=	ext{size}(C_n)$, with $	ext{size}(C_n)+1\le B$. For natural numbers $d,V,k,U,W,K$ such that $V+d=\text{size}(C_n)$, $n\le V$, $k\le i$, $U,W\le B$, and $K=k+|S|\le B$, where $S$ is the encoding of the gates of $C_n$ from index $V-n$ onward, start the gate-processing machine in state $gS$, with registers $(k,V,U,W)$, no recorded answer, and input encoding $1^n$ paired with the binary representation of $i$. If $k\le i<k+|S|$, the machine halts with answer $\text{lm}\lor S_{i-k}$; if $k+|S|\le i$, it reaches a configuration of the form $(oS,K,\text{size}(C_n),U',W',\text{no answer})$ for some $U',W'\le B$. At every earlier step in either case, all four register values are at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: The circuit family and natural numbers $n,i,B$ are fixed; $[?]$ is a Boolean parameter $	ext{lm$.
The gate argument lists of $C_n$ are sorted in strictly increasing order.
$K$ is $k$ plus the length of the encoding of the gates of $C_n$ from index $V-n$ onward.
caveat: The statement’s progress predicate specifies bounded-register reachability and halting only through the provided auxiliary definitions; the displayed configuration description summarizes those predicates.
